headline: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The committee heard testimony on Tutu and Me, housing and water rates, and approved a coral reef grant condition with eight ayes.
meeting.recap: The only agenda item was the proposed fiscal year 27 County of Maui budget.[[0:11:23]] A University of Hawaiʻi researcher asked for 2 million dollars in county co-funding for Hoʻala, a health program.[[0:28:49]] A testifier raised concerns about a proposed top water rate of 19.80 dollars per thousand gallons above 50,000 gallons.[[1:48:04]] A council member moved to add a grant condition for the Maui Ocean Center Marine Institute.[[2:10:19]] The member said the institute grows broken coral pieces and puts them back on the reef.[[2:11:56]] The motion passed with eight ayes and one member excused.[[2:15:06]]
decided: The chair closed public testimony and said written testimony will be accepted.
meeting.next: The chair said member priorities come first, then budget items in the order they appear in Bill 55.

moments.q: Vote on coral reef grant condition

trackerIssues.title: Water rate increases and $19.80 top tier

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: A testifier spoke against the water rates proposed in the budget.
issues.why: He said neighbors got high bills when meters went unread for months and their use fell into the top tier.
issues.next: He asked members to consider his concerns when they reach the water rates.
issues.brief: The proposed top tier is 19.80 dollars per thousand gallons for use over 50,000 gallons.[[#1]] He said that rate is almost 10 times the lowest tier.[[#2]] He said multifamily dwellings are charged a flat 5.09 dollars.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: Members heard requests to keep Affordable Housing Fund projects in the budget.
issues.brief: Department staff said the PARIS rental program received 3 million dollars in FY25.[[#1]] Staff said a grant of a little over 1 million dollars to that program was executed on April 6.[[#2]] The housing director said 13 to 15 applications came in and readiness is the first priority.[[#3]] Staff confirmed a 670,000 dollar contract for Huliao Apartments is no longer needed.[[#4]]

issues.oneLine: Testifiers supported county money for Hoʻala, a planned rural prevention and disaster recovery health system.
issues.why: A testifier said the health effects of the 2023 Maui wildfires are still unfolding years later.
issues.brief: A testifier said the program has included first responders.[[#1]] A University of Hawaiʻi researcher asked for 2 million dollars in county co-funding for Hoʻala.[[#2]] He said the money would help serve 3,000 people through prevention, diagnosis, community navigation and referral to care.[[#3]]
